payload.headline: AMD rebounds 6.85% to 453.46, but still far above every fair-value estimate

summary.thesis: AMD's business is growing fast and getting more profitable, but at 453.46 the price assumes more growth than any of our valuation methods supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no entry while the price sits between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Value buy at 333.38 or lower; swing only on a close above 460.21

payload.happening: AMD rose 6.85% to 453.46. That recovers part of the previous session's drop to 424.39. The price now sits just above the 424.03–451.0 support zone and just below the 460.21–480.33 resistance zone. The only news since the last note is a CNBC piece, reported, about what Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia means for AMD shares. The next earnings report is due 2027-02-02.
payload.business: The rebound and the Nvidia headline change sentiment. They do not change the business. The latest filing (2026-11-04) shows a business in good shape. Trailing sales rose to 45.4B from 32.0B, up 41.87%. Last quarter's sales growth picked up to 44.68% from 37.85% two quarters earlier. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, roughly doubled to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, rose to 7.1B from 5.4B. AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not a concern. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates 11.3% in 30 days. Two things are at risk. First, inventory grew 57% while sales grew 45%; unsold chips can force price cuts. Second, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%. Margins at a peak often come down. Segment data is not available, so we cannot say which product lines drive growth. The competitive effect of Nvidia leadership news is not known from our data.

worth.text: Every method puts fair value well below the price. The cash-flow model (DCF), which values the business on its future free cash flow, gives 145.29 (bear), 186.22 (base) and 220.22 (bull). AMD's own history of price-to-sales gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify the price, free cash flow would need to start growing at 55.7% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, which gives 186.22. At 20% it gives 129.23. Margins matter too: at a 13% operating margin, value falls to 98.25. Multiples tell the same story. The stock trades at 98.9 times trailing earnings and 16.4 times sales, versus a peer median of 10.7 times sales. It sits in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. The only multiple that looks reasonable is 25.7 times next year's earnings. That depends on analysts' next-year EPS of 17.64, which they expect to be roughly double this year's 8.08, coming true.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 55.7% a year, while the model caps it at 30% (186.22 a share), so the gap rests on analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth holding up.

bull: Growth is speeding up: last quarter's sales rose 44.68%, up from 37.85% two quarters earlier.
Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year EPS of 17.64 is up 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the stock at 25.7 times next year's earnings.
Cash is strong: free cash flow is 7.1B and AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt.
bear: At 453.46 the price is above the top of every fair-value method (333.38).
Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, a classic setup for price cuts and lower margins.
At 16.4 times sales, the stock costs more than the 10.7 peer median and sits in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.99–403.47 support zone. A close below it would mean the selloff is deepening, though the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range. The case for buying on value starts here.

longterm.why: The business is improving, but the price needs 55.7% cash-flow growth to make sense, well above the model's 30% cap. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster growth.

swing.why: The price is boxed in between the 424.03–451.0 support and the 460.21–480.33 resistance. It sits above the 200-day average (431.01) but below the 20-day (505.19) and 50-day (552.3) averages, with no trend. The average daily range (ATR) is 45.95, larger than either distance, so no entry until a close above 460.21.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are more than two months away. Options price a 21.3% move by 2026-12-18, and put open interest outweighs calls 2.42 to 1, with the most puts at the 400 strike. More AI-sector or Nvidia headlines could move the price to either zone before the report.

change_mind: A close above 460.21 would show buyers taking the resistance zone and would open a swing entry toward 480.33.
A drop to 333.38 or lower while analysts' next-year EPS stays near 17.64 would turn the long-term call to buy.
If the 2027-02-02 report shows inventory still rising faster than sales (57% vs 45% now) or operating margin falling from 17.72%, the call would move to avoid even at lower prices.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; the 6.85% rebound to 453.46 moved the price further above the 333.38 top of fair value, not closer to it.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
